## Key terms

- Whole-Body Control (WBC) (全身控制)
- Quadratic Programming (QP) (二次规划)
- Model Predictive Control (MPC) (模型预测控制)
- State Estimation (状态估计)
- Unified Robot Description Format (URDF) (统一机器人描述格式)
- Joint Torque (关节力矩)

## Problem and symptoms

- How can we reduce the difficulty of diagnosing issues when migrating an open-source NMPC+WBC framework to a custom robot model?
- Why does the framework not retain the static constraint of the support leg?
- After model replacement, the LQ Approximation in OCS2 SQP accounts for 93.5% of the runtime and the dummy robot is stationary.
- The foot end trajectory is abnormally directed in the custom model; the dummy node does not respond to commands.
- A comment measures the LQ Approximation at 1528.7 ms, which accounts for 93.5049% of the total SQP time.

## Environment

- MuJoCo simulation; OCS2 NMPC; Pinocchio dynamics; qpOASES weighted-QP WBC; SolidWorks export of URDF.

## Priority diagnostics

- First, isolate the MPC using an OCS2 dummy, then use the Cheat Controller to directly read simulation truth values and isolate the state estimator.
- Check the inertial and kinematics of the URDF, foot end kinematic constraints, and the H matrix weights of the weighted-QP.

## Possible causes

- The inertial matrix exported by the SolidWorks URDF plugin may be incorrect.
- The static support leg constraint was causing issues during the author's debugging and was removed; the root cause of the SQP linearization bottleneck has not been confirmed.

## Attempts

- The author first completed the Cheat Controller, then added and stabilized the linear Kalman state estimator.
- The inertial and kinematics parameters were re-filled in SolidWorks using the link coordinate system and negative tensor notation.

## Effective fixes

- For model migration, use a layered validation approach: dummy → Cheat Controller → state estimator, and correct the inertial parameters.

## Result

- The original author reported that the simulation framework can run stably; the support leg constraints and the slow LQ Approximation in the SQP have not been reproduced after the fix.

## Limitations

- The main evidence comes from simulation and the comment section; there is no independent verification of the same process in a real humanoid robot or high-speed motion.

## Safety notes

- Incorrect inertial parameters, contact constraints, or state estimation should not be directly deployed on real machines; they should be validated in dummy and simulation first.
